name: Celestial Rank
reason: The source title 'Heaven Rank' (also rendered 'Sky Rank'), recorded in the Book of Heaven Rank, was localized as 'Celestial Rank' for a grander Western fantasy register.
description: A supreme title displayed by the Talent Tablet before the name of a once-in-an-era genius; Zane earns it inside the Tower of Sin (Eps 601+). It is also the name of an ancient race that is said, in the Book of Celestial Rank, to have once owned the Tower of Sin.

name: Huey
reason: The Chinese name 'Xiu Ye' was localized to the phonetically similar Western name 'Huey'; the source line 'Your demon race once had a peak war reverend called Xiu Ye' maps directly to Ep 664's 'Your people once had a peak War Lord called Huey'.
description: A mythic peak War Lord of Malcolm and Timothy's people (the ogres), whose name was whispered with reverence and dread throughout the Flaming Place and the Dread Place. He suppressed his cultivation at peak War Lord for over a hundred years and single-handedly secured his race's seat in the Tower of Sin; he was later revealed to have been Vesper's puppet, and his disappearance was a huge blow to his race.

name: Feather Emperor's Secret Realm
reason: The source's English term 'Feather Emperor's Secret Realm' was retained verbatim; verified directly in source chapters 773-842.
description: A dangerous secret realm on an island at the center of the four Divine Kingdoms, inside the Sacred Feather Sea. It was originally the mine and forge of the Dragon Bloodline Clan, named for their most famous blacksmith, the Feather Emperor; Zane plans to mine ancient heartstones there (Eps 775-904).

name: Titus
reason: The Chinese name 'Zhan Yun' was localized to the strong classical name 'Titus', fitting a celebrated martial-house champion; the aligned source chapters (ch 764-782) show Zhan Yun as the martial-house star who is publicly defeated, matching Titus's loss in Eps 800-801.
description: A legend of the Wisteria Martial House and a top-tier fighter for the Star Field Divine Kingdom, introduced representing his house before Emperor Scott (Ep 800). Despite his reputation, he is decisively beaten in the arena and left crushed by the defeat (Ep 801).

name: Fiery Shine
reason: The True Phoenix's source name 'Huo Yao' (fire shine) was localized descriptively as 'Fiery Shine', preserving the name's meaning.
description: A True Phoenix and Super Divine Beast bonded to Fiona, treated more as a friend than a servant (Ep 820). It wields the Sun Flame Attack, and it is said that if it ever reached level eleven, matching a Soul Sea Realm warrior, no one in the Divine Kingdoms could stop it.

name: Alexander Shaw
issues: MasterLS hint 'Xander' (Ep 487, Ethereal Spirit Sect) is a DIFFERENT character and should not be merged with Alexander Shaw (Eps 894-895), who is the long-dead Dragon Bloodline Clan leader Feng Xiao.
description: The leader of the Dragon Bloodline Clan from 70,000 years ago (source: Feng Xiao), whose silver-haired corpse still radiates a commanding aura of raw power. His preserved body lies in a coffin on a trial platform; during the soul-possession trial, Scott's soul animates the corpse, which climbs out of its coffin before returning to rest (Eps 894-895).

name: Gilded Gavel
reason: The source's 'Tianlu Auction House' was renamed 'The Gilded Gavel', an evocative Western auction-house name, replacing the Chinese place name.
description: A renowned auction venue, one of the many jewels in its owners' crown and the site of most of the realm's biggest and most legendary auctions (Eps 96-101), including the sale of the weapon-refining manual Zane seeks.

name: Grunts
reason: The source's rank-and-file demon soldiers ('Yao Soldiers') were localized as 'Grunts' (also 'Demonic Grunts'), a plain military term for mindless foot troops.
description: The mindless rank-and-file of the demon horde, fighting in swarms beneath the Demon Commanders. Dozens circle like vultures in battle, and countless Grunts scale the walls of Silverspire during the demon siege (Eps 116-125).

name: Stormcrown Peak
reason: The source's 'Heavenly Fury Peak' was renamed 'Stormcrown Peak', keeping the sky-wrath imagery in a Western fantasy register.
description: One of the peaks of the Skyreach Sect whose apprentices take part in the demon-hunt trial (Eps 118-124). Its group is led by the arrogant Core Apprentice Preston Sterling and clashes repeatedly with Zane and Dalton's party.

name: Demon Core
issues: The name covers two distinct uses in the episodes: the massive core dropped by a slain demonic beast (Ep 148, source 'Monster Core' in ch ~137) and the black energy core wielded by the Netherlord Aldrich (Ep 134); context disambiguates, but the sheet should note both senses.
description: A crystalline core of condensed power left behind when a mighty demonic beast is destroyed; in Ep 148 a massive Demon Core crashes to the earth when the colossal beast vanishes. The term is also used for the black energy core the Netherlord Aldrich forms in battle (Ep 134).

name: Orion
reason: The source's Black Iron Demon King, the demon king Luo Zheng kills in the White Emperor City arc (ch ~126-128), was given the personal name 'Orion' and the localized title 'Dreadlord' (the adaptation's term for Demon King).
description: An antagonist Dreadlord, one of the Four Dreadlords, tied to the Titan's Pillar (Eps 136-138; MasterLS confirms Dreadlord, NOT Netherlord). A monster in combat, he tries to stop Zane from absorbing the Hellfire that is crucial to Aldrich, cutting off the Soul Realm warriors who move to save Yolande Shaw.

name: Storm Panther
reason: The source beast 'Thunder Leopard' (also 'Rushing Thunder Leopard') was renamed 'Storm Panther', a close Western-register equivalent of the lightning-fast cat.
description: A beast famed as the fastest creature in the Eastern Territory (Eps 150-151). Even at a sprint it looks like a tiny ant beside the colossal Automatons, and the episodes use it as the benchmark of pure speed.

name: Earth
reason: Generic element word (one of the five elements: Metal, Wood, Water, Fire, Earth) and a fragment of longer names such as 'Earth Tree' and 'Earth Protection'; not a standalone entity.

name: Tier Five Cultivation Method
reason: Compositional classification phrase ('Tier Five' + 'Cultivation Method') describing the grade of manuals such as the 'Malevolent Cycle of Life and Death'; not a named entity in itself.

name: Augustus
reason: The Daoist appellation 'Zi Qing' (Reverend/Daoist Ziqing) was localized to 'Augustus', a venerable classical name suiting one of the sect's highest-ranking saints; the title 'Zhenren/Reverend' became 'Saint'.
description: One of the ten highest-ranking saints of the Skyreach Sect, an old man who weighs his words carefully over tea (Ep 189). After Saint Viana reports that Zane blocked her Deathly Palm, Augustus dismisses it at first but is persuaded, and the two conspire to eliminate Zane before he can uncover what they did to Elara; he had earlier protected and sponsored a protege's rise within the sect (Eps 277-279).

name: Chillwater Drops
reason: The source technique 'Water Droplets' (ch 173) was renamed 'Chillwater Drops' to give the generic term a distinct ice-technique flavor.
description: Bob of House Pauling's ranged ice technique: thousands of compressed water droplets summoned as a defensive barrage (Eps 185-186). Zane's counterattack vaporizes every last one of them.

name: Falcon's Perch
reason: An adaptation-coined location name with no identifiable source counterpart in the evidence; named for its stake-climbing training challenges.
description: A training peak adjacent to Misty Peak featuring climbing-wall challenges (Ep 190+). Zane sprints from stake to stake and reaches its top in minutes.

name: George
reason: The source character 'Cang Qiu', the white-haired uncle of Zhu Qianning (Ingrid) who saves the protagonist, was localized as 'George'; the surname 'Solomon' ties him to the Solomon Clan (source Family Zhu).
description: A Solomon Clan elder and master of needle and concealed-weapon techniques, the clan's specialty, with gray hair but a young face (Eps 206-208). An anomaly of talent produced by the clan in the last decade, he saves Zane and is addressed as 'Uncle George' by Ingrid, who is close to nearly everyone in House Solomon except him.

name: Nine-Edge Sword
reason: The source sword 'Jiu Zhong Feng' (ch 196), a blade a hundred times heavier than an ordinary sword, was localized as the 'Nine-Edge Sword', preserving the 'nine' of the original name.
description: An extraordinarily heavy sword weighing one hundred times more than an ordinary blade (Eps 209-210). It is so heavy that most warriors would struggle even to lift it, and drawing it produces only a low, grinding scrape.

name: Spirit
reason: Fragment of many unrelated longer terms (Spirit Beasts, Spirit weapon tier, Dragon Spirit, Shadow Palace's Lee, Blood Spirit Race); not a standalone entity.

name: Ninety-Foot Peak
reason: The source's 'Jiuzhang Peak' (nine zhang, roughly ninety feet) was translated literally as 'Ninety-Foot Peak', converting the Chinese unit of measure.
description: A sect division of the Skyreach Sect led by Lady Hawkins, ranked eleventh among the Thirty-Three Peaks and on the rise (Eps 239-284). Its disciples, including the top-ranked Zachary, mistreat Eliot, prompting Zane's silent vow to make Ninety-Foot Peak pay.

name: Grade Two
reason: Generic cultivation sub-level fragment (as in 'Grade Two Adept'); not a standalone entity.

name: Eternal Cycle
reason: The source technique 'Buddha's Reincarnation', used by Pei Tianyao (Patrick) in the aligned chapters, was localized as 'The Eternal Cycle', removing the explicit Buddhist reference while keeping the reincarnation concept.
description: Patrick's signature counterattack technique, tied to his Cosmos philosophy (Ep 280+). Despite its formidable appearance, his incomplete Eternal Cycle crumbles against Wynn's perfected Reaper's Chop (Ep 281).

name: Monastic Path
reason: Patrick's (Pei Tianyao's) Buddhist cultivation path in the source (Acala, Vajra Body, Buddha's Reincarnation) was generalized to the 'Monastic Path', removing explicit religious references for the Western fantasy setting.
description: A secretive and unrivaled cultivation philosophy commanding power that few dare challenge (Ep 281+). Followers like Patrick prize emotional control above even physical strength, and training on this path once made a practitioner stronger than Finn back in the Skyreach Sect.

name: Val
reason: The source's Ice Sword Celestial Being, whose lingering soul controls a Sword Spirit on the sword mountain (ch ~289-306), was given the personal Western name 'Val' in the adaptation.
description: A long-dead sword master whose lingering spirit guards a stretch of the sword ridge (Eps 302-314). Zane, aided by the Malice from his own sword spirit, shatters Val's sword spirit layer by layer to fight his way further up the ridge.

name: Extreme Thunder Sword Intent
reason: The source's English term 'Extreme Thunder Sword Intent' (also 'Extreme Lightning Sword Intent'), the fusion of sword intent with the Law of Thunder, was retained verbatim.
description: Finn's evolved sword technique combining his Celestial Blade with the power of thunder, mastered after the Sword Tempering Pool (Eps 305-307). He infuses it into the Sword of Celestial Judgment, a blade so potent that Patrick had to summon The Immovable Guardian to block it.

name: Shadow
reason: Fragment of many unrelated longer terms (Shadow of the Immovable Guardian, Shadow Palace, Shadow Gnawers, Shadow Fist); not a standalone entity.

name: Silversun Hall
reason: The source's 'Yuxing Palace' (rendered elsewhere as 'Feather Star Hall'), the prince's residence in the aligned chapters, was renamed 'Silversun Hall' for the Western fantasy register.
description: Prince Ray's grand hall with gilded columns and vaulted ceilings, the setting for banquets, political maneuvering, and fight challenges (Eps 338-347). Zane attends as the prince's guest, and the visit ends in a tense, hostile standoff in the courtyard.

name: Uncle Kyle
reason: The source's 'Uncle Ya', the royal elder with dense True Essence who duels the protagonist at the prince's palace (ch 333), was localized as 'Uncle Kyle'.
description: Prince Ray's trusted follower and a royal family elder, short and stocky but surprisingly agile (Eps 345-346). Fighting with a spear and Vitality-infused power, he bats away every one of Zane's attacks in their duel at Silversun Hall.

name: Second-Tier Sect
reason: The source's sect-grading classification (second-rate/second-grade sects) was localized as 'Second-Tier Sect' to fit the adaptation's tiering vocabulary.
description: A rank in the world's sect-grading system denoting sects a level below the great powers (Eps 366-971). The leaders of such sects would barely qualify as assistants in truly elite institutions.

name: Soul Essence
reason: The source material 'Black Nightmare Essence' (chs 376-399) was renamed 'Soul Essence', matching the adaptation's renaming of Black Nightmares to Nether Phantoms.
description: A dark material refined from Nether Phantoms; creating it is the entire reason Nether Phantoms exist on the Cloud Road (Eps 388-400). The black objects fortify the consumer's soul but are dangerous to consume directly, and Zane pairs one with Lifeblood to amplify body and soul together (Ep 416).

name: Son
reason: Generic word and sentence fragment ('Son of a bitch', fragment of 'Son of the Plane'); the meaningful entity would be the full term 'Son of the Plane', not the bare word.
